issues.where: near foreground granulation, bottom third (crops S-W in image-04, D/G in image-02)
issues.what: the granules look like glossy wet plastic or molten caramel. They have hard specular hotspots, a fine scratch-like streak texture inside each cell and a sculpted, airbrushed look. They read as a rendered material, not glowing plasma
issues.fix: remove the specular/gloss term and drive the granules with emissive brightness only (bright cell centres, dark lanes), with softer, smoother intensity inside the cells

issues.where: coronal loops over the sunspot (crops A, C, F, H in image-02; K, L in image-03)
issues.what: the loops are made of thin, sharp, sparkler-like streaks, with spark particles and drips falling from the arcs. They look like long-exposure fireworks or a particle effect, not plasma flux tubes, and the particle origin is obvious
issues.fix: build the loops from fewer, thicker, softly glowing strands with smooth falloff along each tube; drop the falling spark particles and droplet streaks

issues.where: bottom limb of the disc, just left of centre (about x 690-740, y 705-720; crop V in image-08)
issues.what: a small desaturated grey-green smudge sits on the limb. It breaks the orange surface and looks like a texture seam or a stray patch
issues.fix: find the texture seam or bad patch at that spot on the sphere map and paint it out, or rotate the map so the seam is off the visible disc

issues.where: corona all round the disc (crops B, D, E, G, U, V, W in image-06/07/08)
issues.what: the corona streamers are opaque, milky-white brush strokes that start hard at the limb. Some of them overlap the disc edge, and they look painted rather than diffuse and emissive. The bottom streamers in V/U look like smeared paint
issues.fix: make the corona additive and much more transparent, with a radial falloff that starts behind the limb, and use fine filamentary structure instead of broad strokes

issues.where: disc surface (crops A, F, P, Q)
issues.what: the surface texture is a busy, high-frequency mush. It is noisy and somewhat oversharpened, with no clear granulation scale, and it does not darken towards the limb
issues.fix: add limb darkening and use a cleaner granulation/supergranulation texture at a consistent scale; reduce sharpening

issues.where: prominences at left and right limb (crops C, D, E, H, M, O)
issues.what: the prominences are saturated red ribbons with hard, cut-out edges, sitting on top of the corona like a pasted layer
issues.fix: soften the prominence edges, raise their emissive glow and blend them additively with the corona

issues.where: upper limb behind the loops (crops I, N, O in image-02/03)
issues.what: the spicule fringe along the horizon is a uniform comb of short hairs, repeated evenly along the limb
issues.fix: vary the length, density and brightness of the spicules along the limb

issues.where: sky, upper left (crops B, J, K)
issues.what: a Milky Way band is visible behind the Sun's close-up limb, and there is a dense star field right up against a blindingly bright surface. It holds up at native size, but it looks like a stock backdrop
issues.fix: dim the star field and the galactic band close to the bright limb, or remove them

issues.where: crop V (912,866,456,214), southern solar globe just inside the bottom limb (also visible at bottom of disk in image-09.png)
issues.what: equirectangular UV pole pinching and concentric swirling compress the solar surface texture into a desaturated pale point surrounded by stretched rings
issues.fix: use cube-sphere, triplanar, or polar-patched mapping on the solar globe so surface detail stays isotropic all the way to the poles without pinching

issues.where: crops B, C, D, E, and G across the inner corona, spicule rim, and prominences (also in image-11.png crops K, L, M, P, R)
issues.what: crisp 1-2 px white star dots shine unattenuated through the bright inner corona, 1-2 px off the limb over chromospheric spicules, and directly on top of opaque red prominence plasma (e.g., lower-right prominence base in crop E and upper-right loop in crop C), exposing an unmasked additive star layer
issues.fix: occlude the starfield behind the solar disk, spicule fringe, and prominence alpha, and extinguish stars smoothly within the bright coronal glare

issues.where: crops H and I along the left and right Milky Way bands (also in image-11.png crops J, O, R and image-12.png crop S)
issues.what: the Milky Way background bitmap is soft and visibly upscaled at native size with smeared 4-7 px baked-in star blobs (including diagonally stretched blobs near the top-left of crop J) clashing against sharp 1-2 px procedural stars stamped on top
issues.fix: use a higher-resolution starless Milky Way dust/nebula map at native pixel scale and generate all stars with a consistent anti-aliased point-spread profile

issues.where: crops C, D, and E along thin outer prominence filaments and the equatorial solar limb
issues.what: fine outer prominence tendrils break into 1 px stair-stepped segments and isolated pixels at native scale, and the equatorial photospheric edge meets the spicule fringe in a slightly hard 1-2 px bright rim line
issues.fix: supersample thin prominence filaments and soften the radial opacity falloff across the photosphere-to-chromosphere limb boundary
